findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: The Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback now does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If that array is empty or missing, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and this throws before any event is created. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so bookings with no destination calendar and a Google Meet location now fail instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Organizer email is always the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent (and updateEvent) set the Google organizer attendee email from `destinationCalendar[0]`, while the calendar written to is chosen by `credentialId`. For a collective booking EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential with the full destination array, so every host's event is created with the first host's calendar id as the organizer email. Secondary hosts can fail Google insert/update or get an event owned by the wrong identity, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Update/delete no longer fall back to a destination calendar
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. That comparison is against a falsy id, so it never matches, and `calendarId` becomes undefined. Previously this fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates and deletes for bookings that have no stored external calendar id (or a null one) are sent to Google without a calendar id and fail, leaving stale events.

findings.title: Lark still writes only the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent, and deleteEvent all take `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` and ignore the credential CalendarManager now passes in. On a collective event that array starts with the organizer, so a co-host's Lark credential tries to create or delete on the organizer's calendar id and throws "no calendar id" or a permission error. The co-host never gets their own Lark event. Office 365 createEvent and the CalDAV base service have the same first-element-only behavior, so any non-Google host is not actually supported.

findings.title: Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar, and the collective branch then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Optional chaining no-ops on null, so every co-host calendar collected above is discarded. Those hosts are not invited on their calendars even though they have destination calendars configured — the exact failure this PR describes — whenever the organizer has no destination calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancel deletes the same event with every credential
findings.body: The new loop walks every calendar booking reference, and the all-remaining recurring branch ignores that reference's credential. For each reference it loads every user calendar credential and, for each updated booking, deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`) with that credential. One recurring series cancel therefore issues duplicate deletes of the same event id against unrelated calendars, and never targets the other hosts' references. Later instances can be left on calendars or the cancel promise set can fail.

findings.title: updateEvent is called with an undefined credential
findings.body: If a calendar reference has a credentialId that is not on the EventManager user and the DB lookup misses (or the credential has no app slug), `credential` stays undefined, but the code still pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`. getCalendar(undefined) throws, the surrounding catch returns failure for every reference, and remaining hosts' calendar events are not updated. createAllCalendarEvents guards this with `if (credential)`; the update path does not.

findings.title: Organization slug assignment flag is inverted
findings.body: This unrelated change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` while still writing `requestedSlug` only when billing is enabled. With billing off, the new organization is created with no slug, so its URL does not resolve. With billing on, slug is set immediately instead of only `requestedSlug`, skipping the billing gate the old condition enforced. Organization creation is broken in both configurations.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is now inconsistent
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single object or null to an array, and handlers do not agree on the empty value: confirm/cancel send `[]`, while other payloads still emit `null` (the BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook tests still expect null; only BOOKING_REJECTED was updated to []). Subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.integration` or `externalId` will throw, and clients cannot rely on one type. The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a webhook contract change.
